title: E-commerce Store & Admin Dashboard
subtitle: A complete online jewellery store, with orders, payments and returns run from a phone.
_comment_package: It is 'WhatsApp Store' again, and this time that is CORRECT rather than a
regression. It was renamed to 'Shop Starter' when the only published tier
near it was Starter Store at ₹99,000 — a 2.5x contradiction a client could
find with one search. The published tier list now opens at WhatsApp Store,
₹49,999 over 4 weeks, and that tier IS this product: storefront, checkout,
Razorpay with COD, orders, admin, and the WhatsApp desk as the back office.
Customer accounts and OTP sit in this quote's add-ons for the same reason
they sit in Starter — they are the operations layer, one tier up.
So the quote and the site now agree by construction instead of by luck,
which is the entire point of the tiers. tools/quote-doc.mjs enforces the
terms of that reuse: published list price exactly, never longer than the
published length, and the payable price at or below list.
_comment_price: PRICE SET BY SUMANTH, deliberately, with the floor argument heard and
overruled. ₹39,999 over 15 working days is ₹2,666/day against a ₹8,000
floor. The reasons are commercial and they are his to weigh: the studio is
short of leads, this is cash now, and the add-ons page is the way back in.
ANCHOR CHANGED ₹59,999 -> ₹49,999, and the discount is therefore ₹10,000
rather than ₹20,000. ₹59,999 was a number that appeared nowhere — not on
the site, not in bm-app.js, not in any structured data. An invented list
price on a document sent to a client is a false statement about the
studio's own pricing, which is the same class of thing §4 forbids on an
invoice. ₹49,999 is published, and a client who checks finds it and sees a
real discount. A smaller anchor that survives being checked is worth more
than a larger one that does not.
To restore the bigger strike-through, raise listPrice — but the tool will
then require the package to carry its own name again.
_comment_lineItems: Rebalanced to sum to the ₹49,999 list price, not the old ₹59,999. The tool
refuses to render a quote whose own arithmetic does not add up, and a
client adds the column up. The proportions are unchanged; ₹10,000 came off
across the build lines rather than out of any single one.

stages.name: Kick-off
stages.what: We collect your product list, photographs, descriptions, WhatsApp number and business details.

stages.name: Design
stages.what: Home, product and checkout screens for your approval. Two rounds of revisions are included here — this is where changes are cheap.

stages.name: Build
stages.what: Storefront, admin dashboard, database and payments. Your catalogue loaded with real photographs, prices and stock.

stages.name: Review
stages.what: A private staging link. You place test orders, we fix what you find, and we walk you through the dashboard on a call.

stages.name: Launch
stages.what: Domain pointed, payment keys switched to live, sample data cleared. The shop is open.

_comment_carePlan: REMOVED from this quote, not repriced. Care is published at ₹12,500/mo and
that is the number the tool reads — a quote cannot type a cheaper one, which
is how ₹2,500 got into the last draft. But ₹12,500/mo beside a ₹39,999 build
is a bigger monthly ask than the build itself and would stall the close.
So it is simply not offered here. The 30-day warranty still applies, and the
add-ons page is the way back in.
_comment_hourly: The hourly rate is GONE. The SOW template says the studio does not bill by
the hour, and ₹900/hr was ₹7,200/day — under the floor again.
notIncluded: Drafting or reviewing your legal policies

_comment_weeks: Back to Sumanth's original 3 weeks. Five weeks made the day rate worse
(same money, more days) and delayed the cash this is being taken for.
He knows how much of the existing demo build is reusable; I do not.
